seo.metaTitle: Silhouette PNG - Turn Image Into A Solid Shape
seo.metaDescription: Turn any image into a flat silhouette in your browser: every visible pixel becomes one solid color while transparency is kept. Free, no upload.
seo.longDescription: Make a silhouette flattens an image into its outline: every pixel that is visible becomes one solid color of your choice, while fully transparent areas stay transparent and partially transparent edges keep their own alpha — so a cut-out logo stays a cut-out instead of becoming a filled rectangle. A threshold decides how faint a pixel may be and still count as part of the shape; raising it eats away at soft, anti-aliased edges. This is a shape filter, not a background remover: it does not find the subject, it takes everything you already have visible. Everything runs locally in your browser.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Every visible pixel is repainted one solid color; only alpha survives.
Soft edges keep their own alpha — the cut-out stays a cut-out.
A threshold too high punches holes in anti-aliased edges.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Pick the fill color for the shape.
Set the threshold: pixels fainter than it are treated as empty.
Download the result as a transparent PNG.

faq.q: What exactly happens to the colors?
faq.a: They are gone: every visible pixel is repainted in the fill color you picked. Only the alpha channel survives, so the result shows the outline of what was there.

faq.q: Does it keep my transparent background?
faq.a: Yes. Fully transparent pixels are skipped, and partially transparent ones keep their own alpha, so soft edges and shadows survive as a soft edge rather than a hard step.

faq.q: Why did the outline get holes in it?
faq.a: The threshold is too high. Pixels with low alpha were treated as empty and dropped, which happens first on anti-aliased and semi-transparent edges. Lower it until the shape is solid again.

faq.q: Is this a background removal tool?
faq.a: No. It does not look for a subject: whatever was already visible becomes the shape. To isolate one object first, cut it out with the remove background or extract color tools, then run the silhouette on the result.
